cards.title: Your Smart Devices Are Being Held Hostage: The Local AI Escape Plan
cards.thesis: People are fed up with their smart devices and software becoming useless or more expensive because companies kill off apps or change terms. There's a growing demand for products that run locally, are open-source, or give users more control, especially as powerful AI models can now run directly on personal devices like Macs and iPhones, making cloud dependence unnecessary.

evidence.text: I built a specialized engine for running a powerful AI model (Gemma 4 26B) on any M-series Mac using only 2 GB of RAM. I've always loved on-device AI; it feels like magic to run a powerful neural network right on your Mac or iPhone.
Keychron, a popular keyboard and mouse brand, announced the first open-source firmware for their gaming mice, giving users more control and customization options.

My old Belkin smart switch became unusable because the company turned off its app. I managed to get it working again without their app, but it shows how frustrating it is when a product you own stops working because a company discontinues its software.
There's growing discussion about why the future of software development points towards more local applications, which run directly on your device rather than relying on remote servers.

Companies like Tokenless are building tools to automatically switch between different AI models to save on costs, showing that the expense of using cloud-based AI is a major concern for many businesses.

cards.opportunity: Everyone's complaining about smart devices dying when the company pulls the plug — but nobody's made it easy for non-technical people to flash open-source firmware or run local AI models on them. Imagine a drag-and-drop tool for popular smart plugs or sensors that lets you load a community-built local control app or even a tiny AI agent, completely cutting out the cloud. Ship a no-code solution that turns dead smart tech into locally-controlled, AI-powered gems, and you'll own the frustrated-user market.
